short: Twelve years, four elections, a depression and a world war.
full:
Roosevelt took office in March 1933 with a quarter of the workforce unemployed and the banking system shut. The first hundred days produced fifteen major acts, among them bank rescue, the Civilian Conservation Corps, farm price supports and the Tennessee Valley Authority, and the pace continued with Social Security and the Wagner Act in 1935. The Supreme Court struck down parts of the programme; his attempt to enlarge the court in 1937 failed and cost him support in Congress.

He was elected four times, breaking Washington's two-term precedent, which the Twenty-second Amendment closed in 1951. From 1939 he moved a reluctant country towards the Allies through Lend-Lease and the Atlantic Charter, and from December 1941 directed the largest war effort in history. He died of a cerebral haemorrhage at Warm Springs on 12 April 1945, four weeks before Germany surrendered.
